(Distributive law) Prove that $(x\oplus y)\odot z=x\odot z\oplus y\odot z$ for all $x,y,z\in\mathbb R\cup\{\infty\}$.

hmmt-feb-2008-team2-05.prompt:
A *juggling sequence* of length $n$ is a sequence $j(0)j(1)\dots j(n-1)$ of $n$ nonnegative integers such that the map $f:\mathbb Z\to\mathbb Z$, $f(t)=t+j(\bar t)$, is a permutation of the integers, where $\bar t$ denotes the remainder of $t$ modulo $n$. The sequence has $b$ *balls* if $f$ has exactly $b$ infinite orbits (the orbit of $t$ is $\{t,f(t),f(f(t)),\dots\}$). Think of $j(t)$ as the height of the throw at time $t$: the ball comes back to the hand at time $t+j(t)$.

Prove that $572$ (that is, $j(0)=5$, $j(1)=7$, $j(2)=2$, $n=3$) is not a juggling sequence.
